reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 shows aging-induced softening due to interstitial depletion, not brittle fracture from homogeneous lattice distortion. E2 and E3 discuss eutectic HEAs with pre-existing lamellar phases and interphase boundary strengthening, but provide no evidence that introducing nanophase boundaries into an initially single-phase alloy enhances toughness or that a single-phase HEA fails by cleavage due to restricted slip.
premises: Homogeneous lattice distortion in single-phase HEA restricts slip system activation and impedes dislocation multiplication
Lack of microstructural heterogeneity limits alternative plasticity mechanisms (e.g., transformation-induced plasticity, crack tip shielding)
Introducing nanophase boundaries mediates stress redistribution and promotes dislocation pile-up, enhancing toughness
Under high strain rate/low temperature, single-phase HEA suffers localized stress concentration leading to cleavage fracture
Thermally induced nanophase separation creates interphase boundaries that provide crack tip shielding
